title: TFET gatekeeper fused in series with a MOSFET access channel
idea: One wordline gates a single channel with a p+ tunnel-junction segment next to the storage node and a conventional n+ MOSFET segment toward the bitline. In the off state the band-to-band tunnel junction blocks with a steep (<40 mV/dec) turn-off, and in the on state the MOSFET segment supplies the drive current.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): about 100x lower off-current at the same on-current. The refresh interval goes from 64 ms to seconds, cutting refresh energy by ~90%.

title: Wide-gap oxide drain pocket on a silicon access transistor
idea: The storage-node contact is an IGZO or Ga2O3 landing pad that forms the drain extension, so the high-field drain edge where GIDL is generated lies in >3 eV-gap material while the channel stays silicon for mobility.
why: Band-to-band GIDL dominates the leakage tail under negative-wordline bias, and a wide gap suppresses it exponentially. That could push the 13 fA tail below 0.1 fA, about 10x longer retention.

title: Refresh activations double as in-DRAM copy and zeroing
idea: Fuse refresh with RowClone/Ambit-style bulk operations. The controller queues pending page-zeroing, page-copy and scrub-repair work against rows that are due for refresh, and runs each in the same ACT-ACT-PRE that restores the row.
why: Turns the ~46 fJ/bit refresh cost into useful work and absorbs OS zero and copy traffic (5-10% of bandwidth on VM-dense hosts). Net refresh overhead roughly halves.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO layer inside the buried-wordline gate stack
idea: Put a thin ferroelectric HZO film in series with the high-k gate dielectric of the buried-channel access transistor. Its negative capacitance amplifies gate-to-channel coupling and gives a sub-60 mV/dec subthreshold slope.
why: Allows Vt to rise ~200 mV at the same on-current, for 50-100x lower subthreshold leakage. Alternatively it lets the 3 V wordline boost drop (fact 10).

title: FeRAM-style driven plate line biases cells during retention
idea: Segment the DRAM cell plate per subarray and drive it as FeRAM does. On entering standby, the plate steps so every storage node couples toward the bitline precharge level, which shrinks |Vds| and the junction field, and it steps back before the first ACT.
why: Subthreshold and junction or GIDL leakage are exponential in field and Vds, so self-refresh retention improves 2-5x. Idle power falls 10-20%.

title: Share the accelerator cold-plate loop with HBM and DIMMs
idea: Extend the GPU liquid-cooling cold plates over HBM stacks and DIMMs to hold the arrays at 30-40 C instead of 85-95 C. Thermal sensors then step the refresh multiplier down from 2x to 0.25x.
why: Retention roughly doubles per 10 C, so 16-20x more retention headroom. The 10-20% refresh bandwidth loss falls below 1% and refresh energy drops ~90%.

title: Flash charge-trap layer for per-cell access-transistor Vt trimming
idea: Add a thin nitride charge-trap film to the access-transistor gate stack (SONOS fused with DRAM). At wafer test, retention-profile every cell, then Fowler-Nordheim program electrons into only the leakiest access devices to raise their Vt by 0.2-0.4 V permanently.
why: Refresh rate is set by the top 0.01-0.1% leakage tail. Trimming those cells lets the whole array refresh at median retention, 64 ms to ~1 s, cutting refresh energy ~90%.

title: Oxide retention gate in series with a fast silicon access transistor
idea: Put an oxide-semiconductor transistor in series with each Si access device, driven by a per-bank retention line. That line stays on while the bank is active, so it adds no switching delay, and turns off when the bank idles; the Si device does all the fast switching.
why: Keeps DDR timing in active mode while idle banks reach oxide-level leakage (~1e-19 A). Self-refresh in idle (16-33% of idle power) disappears.

title: Back gate merged as a second, slow wordline
idea: Build the array on UTBB FD-SOI with a ground plane per row group. Hold the plane strongly negative while the group is retaining (Vt +0.3-0.5 V) and swing it toward neutral only for the group being activated.
why: Decoupling on-current from off-leakage gives ~100x less subthreshold leakage. It also lets the wordline boost fall from 3 V toward 2 V, about 55% less CV^2 (fact 10).

title: Nanoelectromechanical contact in series with each access transistor
idea: A monolithic BEOL TiN or CNT cantilever relay sits between the access transistor and the storage node. The same wordline field pulls it in, and it springs open during retention to leave an air gap.
why: The off-state leakage path is a vacuum or air gap, so retention is limited only by capacitor-dielectric leakage and refresh is eliminated for most data. Nanosecond closure and contact wear are unproven.

title: Compressed packing fills freed rows with leak-aligned padding
idea: The controller compresses pages, packs them into fewer rows, and writes the freed rows entirely with each cell type's leak-direction value (0 for true cells, 1 for anti-cells). A per-row flag marks those rows refresh-exempt until reallocated.
why: With ~2x compressibility, 40-50% of rows need no refresh, cutting refresh energy ~40%, and the same packing also yields capacity.

title: Compiler tensor liveness wired into per-row refresh skip
idea: The ML compiler already knows every tensor's lifetime. It tags buffers whose last read comes within the guaranteed retention window (activations in the decode loop, gradient staging, temp scratch), and the controller sets per-row no-refresh bits until they are freed.
why: Refresh bandwidth and energy fall in proportion to the ephemeral share of the footprint, often 30-60% in training and inference.

title: Adiabatic resonant charging for refresh wordlines and bitline restore
idea: Fuse adiabatic logic with refresh bursts. A stepwise or LC-resonant supply ramps the 3 V wordlines and restore drivers, and charge from the row being closed is recycled into the next row opened.
why: Recovers 50-70% of refresh CV^2 energy, roughly 46 to 20 fJ/bit (facts 3 and 10).

title: Silicon carbide cell array hybrid-bonded to silicon periphery
idea: Build the access transistors and storage junctions in 4H-SiC (Eg 3.26 eV) and hybrid-bond the array to a Si CMOS periphery wafer.
why: Junction generation leakage scales with intrinsic carrier density, which is ~1e-8 cm^-3 in SiC against ~1e10 in Si. That allows refresh-free, hour-scale retention, and SiC substrate supply is expanding in the U.S. through EV demand.

title: Antiferroelectric capacitor that switches to nonvolatile mode for sleep
idea: Use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor: high-k and non-remanent in DRAM mode. On sleep, a plate-line offset bias (as in work-function-engineered AFE memory) parks the loop so two polarization states hold with no power, and wake reads them back.
why: Removes self-refresh in standby (16-33% of idle power) and gives instant wake, while active-mode endurance stays unlimited.

title: Erasure decoding serves reads that collide with refresh
idea: Stagger refresh so only one chip in a rank refreshes at a time. A read that hits the refreshing chip is reconstructed from the other chips plus the ECC/parity chip, the way a RAID degraded read works.
why: Hides refresh stalls (10-20% bandwidth and tail latency at 32-64 Gb) using parity that ECC DIMMs already carry.

title: Junctionless gate-all-around access continuous with the storage electrode
idea: Channel and storage node are one uniformly n+ doped nanowire, turned off by full depletion from a gate-all-around wordline. There is no metallurgical pn junction at the storage node.
why: Removes junction leakage and the abrupt-junction GIDL hotspot, which may give a 10-100x lower tail at sub-10 nm wire diameters.

title: Idle bitlines parked at the subarray's majority stored level
idea: Write logic keeps a per-row inversion flag so most cells in a subarray hold the same level. In idle, bitlines park at that rail instead of VDD/2, so majority cells see Vds~0 and subthreshold current, proportional to 1-exp(-Vds/kT), collapses.
why: More than 80% of cells see near-zero leakage drive, extending retention 3-5x and cutting self-refresh energy proportionally.

title: Unified charge-debt counter for retention and row hammer
idea: Each row carries one counter that accumulates time weighted by temperature plus neighbor activations weighted by coupling. A row is refreshed when its debt crosses a threshold, so one mechanism handles both retention and hammer.
why: Replaces the fixed 64 ms sweep plus separate TRR. Quiet rows refresh 4-8x less often, and hammer victims (fact 9, ~1k ACTs) are restored exactly in time.

title: Retention-binned page allocator matches data lifetime to row strength
idea: Profile each row's retention class at test and store the map in SPD. The OS places frequently rewritten data in weak rows and long-lived data in strong rows, each class refreshed at its own rate.
why: Multi-rate refresh is normally capped by weak rows holding long-lived data. Matching them removes that cap and cuts refresh operations 70-80%.

title: Piezoelectric liner strains the access channel during retention
idea: Wrap the buried wordline in an AlScN piezoelectric liner on a separate standby bias. While rows retain, the liner compresses the channel and strain raises Vt; strain is released for access.
why: A strain-tuned Vt shift of 50-100 mV gives 5-20x less leakage with no on-current penalty.

title: Vacuum nanogap field-emission access device
idea: Replace the semiconductor channel with a ~10 nm vacuum gap between a sharpened storage-node tip and the bitline electrode, gated by the wordline (a vacuum tube fused into the cell). It conducts only by gate-assisted field emission.
why: No junction, BTBT or diffusion current exists in the off state, so leakage is near zero and the cell is radiation hard.

title: On-die microheaters anneal variable-retention-time defects in situ
idea: Borrow PCM-style TiN heaters under each subarray. After migrating the subarray's data, pulse it to 300-400 C for microseconds to milliseconds to re-passivate hydrogen-related traps behind the VRT and leakage tail.
why: VRT forces a 2-4x refresh guardband. Periodic healing shrinks the tail so the refresh interval can grow 2-4x over the part's life.

title: Pinned-photodiode storage well from 180 nm image-sensor fabs
idea: Fuse the CIS 4T pixel with a DRAM cell. Charge sits in a fully depleted buried n-well whose surface is pinned by p+, away from the Si/SiO2 interface, and is read by a transfer gate onto a floating diffusion and source follower. This is built on existing 180 nm CIS lines.
why: Pinned-well dark current is ~10 e-/s against ~1e5 e-/s for DRAM junctions, so retention runs seconds to minutes with no refresh. The read is gain-based and non-destructive.

title: Weak-row CAM companion die on the DIMM buffer
idea: A 180 nm CAM-plus-timer die, or a block in the RCD buffer, holds the addresses of the ~0.1% weak rows found at test. It issues targeted extra refreshes for them while the DRAM runs at a 4-8x lower base refresh rate.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth fall 75-85%, and a legacy node is enough for a ~10k-entry CAM.

title: EEPROM high-voltage module builds a thick-oxide, high-Vt access transistor
idea: Use the 1990s EEPROM HV process: 12-15 nm gate oxide, Vt ~1.3 V and channels of 0.5 um or more. EEPROM charge pumps boost the wordline to 5-6 V.
why: Off-leakage of ~1e-18 A gives minute-scale retention, so refresh is negligible. It trades density for a refresh-free tier made in any legacy fab.

title: Vertical NPN gain cell with storage on the floating base
idea: A BiCMOS cell puts the storage node on the floating base of a vertical bipolar transistor under the MOS access gate. A read pulses the emitter so collector current amplifies the stored charge by beta, roughly non-destructively.
why: A gain of 50-100 lets sub-fF residual charge be sensed, tolerating ~10x more decay before refresh, and it removes most restore energy.

title: Electrometer guard bootstrap shields the write transistor
idea: A 4T gain cell has two series write transistors. The source-follower read transistor drives their middle node to track the storage voltage, as a guarded electrometer input does, so the inner device sees Vds~0. This fits a 250-180 nm logic process.
why: Subthreshold current, proportional to 1-exp(-Vds/kT), falls ~100x, giving long retention without a special material.

title: Loadless four-transistor cell held by access-leakage balance
idea: Cross-coupled NMOS drivers with PMOS access devices: in standby, the PMOS off-leakage feeds the high node and outweighs the driver leakage, so the cell latches statically with no refresh (as NEC demonstrated at 180 nm).
why: Refresh-free, ~10 ns access with no capacitor module, buildable in any U.S. legacy logic fab at ~2/3 the area of 6T SRAM.

title: Floating-gate shadow block behind each DRAM subarray
idea: A double-poly EEPROM block behind each subarray acts as a nonvolatile shadow (nvSRAM fused with DRAM). Before power-down, rows stream through the sense amps into the shadow and refresh stops; on wake the shadow restores them, and shadowing can be limited to an OS-state slice.
why: Standby refresh energy falls to zero for edge devices that sit idle for hours, and a 1990s EEPROM flow is enough.

title: Recirculating CCD loops hold streamed model weights
idea: Buried-channel CCD loops built on 350-180 nm CCD lines hold weights that circulate continuously past a regenerating sense-and-restore stage. Each pass taps the stream out to compute at fixed cadence.
why: Refresh is intrinsic to circulation and there are no row decoders (periphery is 49% of the die, fact 7). The cell is ~4F^2 CCD gates, suiting sequential weight streaming.

title: Token-cadence weight reads replace auto-refresh
idea: In LLM decode every weight row is activated each token (20-50 ms). A 180 nm controller or FPGA marks weight banks as refreshed by access, suppresses auto-refresh while cadence stays inside the retention window, and falls back to auto-refresh when traffic stalls.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth for the weight region drop to zero, recovering the 10-20% bandwidth tax at 32-64 Gb with no new silicon.

title: LCD active-matrix backplane repurposed as bulk dynamic memory
idea: An LCD pixel is already a 1T1C DRAM cell refreshed at 60 Hz. Depreciated Gen-2/3 a-Si or LTPS lines (2-4 um rules) could pattern huge TFT-capacitor arrays with on-glass sense amps, and very wide rows offset the microsecond row time.
why: Attacks capital intensity, since those lines cost ~1/100 per area, and avoids EUV entirely. Density and latency are far below DRAM, so it fits only as a wide, slower bulk tier.

title: Canary rows with undersized capacitors gate refresh timing
idea: A mask change gives a few rows per subarray ~70% of normal capacitance, and they are written with a known pattern. A background sampler issues refresh only when canaries start to flip, so the rate tracks real temperature, voltage and aging.
why: 64 ms is a worst-case guardband while typical retention is seconds, so 4-10x fewer refreshes are possible safely.

title: Antifuse redundancy sized for one-second retention binning
idea: Run deep retention tests on 1990s ATE to find rows failing a 1 s retention target. Antifuses remap them to an enlarged spare pool (3-5% spare rows), and the part ships with a 1 s refresh.
why: Refresh energy falls ~94% for a few percent of area.

title: Gated-diode storage amplifies its own charge on read
idea: Replace the capacitor with a planar MOS gated diode. A stored 1 keeps it inverted, so a gate pulse boosts its voltage 3-5x; a stored 0 leaves it depleted with little boost. This fits a 180 nm logic flow.
why: Smaller residual charge still senses correctly, giving a 3-5x longer refresh interval without a high-k capacitor.

title: SIMOX buried oxide under the storage diffusion
idea: Build cells on 1990s SIMOX SOI so the storage n+ sits directly on buried oxide, shrinking its pn junction to a thin sidewall. A body tie suppresses floating-body bipolar leakage.
why: Junction leakage area falls ~90%, giving a 5-10x longer retention tail for the same cell.

title: Second-reference sense amp flags decaying cells during refresh
idea: Each refresh fires an extra comparator with a tighter reference (~60% of a full 1). Rows with cells below it go to a small fast-refresh list, and the base rate slows until flags appear.
why: Online, self-calibrating multi-rate refresh that catches VRT cells, with 60-80% fewer refreshes, using circuits from the 1990s.

title: Legacy-node always-on island lets modern DRAM fully power down
idea: Put a 32-64 MB refresh-free die on the package (180 nm thick-oxide or loadless cells) holding page tables, kernel and wake state. Modern DRAM banks then enter deep power-down with no refresh when idle, flushing or discarding their contents.
why: Idle refresh power (16-33%) goes to near zero for phones and lightly loaded servers, and U.S. legacy fabs make the island.

title: Retention-certified DRAM grades sold at a premium
idea: Use legacy test flows to bin dies by measured retention (256 ms, 1 s at 45 C) and program the refresh setting into SPD. Long-retention bins go to battery devices; leaky bins go to cooled data centers.
why: Monetizes the existing retention spread with zero capex, cutting refresh energy ~75% in the premium segment.

title: Retention rejects rewired as twin-cell half-density parts
idea: A fuse or metal-option mode pairs each cell with its bitline-pair neighbor storing the complement (2T2C). That doubles the sense signal and extends retention ~10x, so dies that would be scrapped sell at half density.
why: Raises usable supply from yield-loss wafers using only legacy fuse and test tools.

title: Thin p-epi on p+ substrate with buried sink drains leakage
idea: Fuse the CCD vertical-overflow-drain design with DRAM. Storage nodes sit in thin, lightly doped epi over a heavily doped, short-lifetime substrate, plus an n-buried layer biased as a carrier sink that removes thermally generated charge before it reaches storage nodes.
why: The diffusion leakage component, which dominates at 85 C, falls ~10x, giving 3-5x hot retention.

title: Tunnel-diode latch pair inside a one-transistor cell
idea: Two series resonant or Si/SiGe interband tunnel diodes on the storage node (a Goto pair, after TI's late-1990s TSRAM) create two stable voltages held by picoamp current. Access uses a standard DRAM transistor.
why: Refresh-free at near-1T1C area, since the diodes stack vertically, costing ~1 mW per Gb of holding power.

title: Detector-grade float-zone silicon cuts generation leakage and quartz dependence
idea: Build DRAM on crucible-free float-zone wafers of the kind used for radiation detectors, with ms-scale minority lifetime and very low metal content, nitrogen-doped for strength. FZ tops out at 200 mm, which suits 1990s tool sets.
why: SRH generation current scales with ni/tau, so junction leakage falls 3-10x. It also bypasses the Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible chokepoint (>80%).

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal hardens interfaces against the leakage tail
idea: Replace the final forming-gas anneal with a high-pressure deuterium furnace anneal, a 1990s hot-carrier fix. Si-D bonds resist breaking far better than Si-H, so fewer interface traps form to drive trap-assisted GIDL and VRT.
why: Shrinks the VRT and tail population 2-5x, allowing a 2x longer refresh interval for one cheap furnace step.

title: Floating negative wordlines replace standby charge pumps
idea: In self-refresh, a single capacitive kick (domino-precharge style) drives all idle wordlines to about -0.6 V, after which they float and their own capacitance holds the bias, topped up rarely by a tiny timer.
why: Keeps the 10-100x leakage benefit of a negative wordline without the static power of an always-on negative pump, cutting standby current 20-30%.
